analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and one paragraph about the Qwen27 TP assistant setup at about line 2456. Both change hunks fall outside the two supplied base excerpts, which cover lines 386-1236, so the actual edits could not be seen here. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the visible part shows only documentation text.

The edit describes `darkbloom cluster local` serving the embedded assistant. It says plain `darkbloom cluster` plans without the assistant under the default `auto`, because the assistant is not qualified for public traffic. It says explicit `on` keeps the assistant but the pair is then not offered to the coordinator.

This is a documentation-only change with no code, control or config change. It does not touch the trust boundaries, attestation, token handling, cache storage (T-041) or the add-on hold socket (TB-012). If anything, the described behavior is conservative: it keeps the unqualified assistant off coordinator-served traffic. I could not verify that the code enforces this. Whether the cluster code actually withholds the pair from the coordinator when `mtp_mode` is `on` is outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that against the cluster and provider sources if the claim matters. I examined the base text in the supplied excerpts (logout, token revocation, sandbox installer, addon hold and stop/restart docs), which are unchanged by this PR, and found no new regression.
